name: Datum Mesh
tagline: Finite-element analysis on the desktop: stresses, deflections and temperatures in parts and frames.
for: Mechanical, structural, process and aerospace engineers, students and lecturers.
about: Datum Mesh finds the stresses, deflections and temperatures in parts and structures by the finite-element method. You draw a frame of beams and truss bars, or the outline of a part with its holes, put on the supports and loads, and solve.

Version 0.1.0 is the first step: the window, the drawing canvas with snap and rulers, frames and parts with supports and loads, materials and sections, worked examples, printing and updates. Solving frames arrives in 0.1.1, meshing and solving parts in 0.1.2, heat conduction, the materials library and the verification report in 0.1.3. Every result will be checked against known answers, and the checks are listed in the app.

steps.title: Draw and mesh
steps.text: Draw a frame of beams and truss bars, or the outline of a part with its holes, on a grid with snap and rulers.

steps.title: Load and support
steps.text: Put supports, forces, pressures, gravity and heat on nodes, members and edges, and set their values with units.

steps.title: Solve and report
steps.text: Solve, read the deflections, stresses and temperatures, and print a report with the equilibrium check.

highlights: Frames and trusses: draw members on a grid, choose sections (rectangle, round bar, tube, box, I, channel, angle) and see their properties
Parts: rectangles, circles and polygons with arcs, and holes cut out of them
Supports and loads on nodes, members and edges: fixed, pinned, rollers, springs, symmetry; forces, moments, distributed loads, pressure, gravity
Heat: fixed temperatures, heat flux, convection and heat generation
SI or US units shown everywhere; files keep SI, so switching never rounds anything
Six worked examples: a portal frame, a roof truss, a lifting lug, an L-bracket with a fillet, a flange plate and a heat sink
Print to PDF with a title block; updates itself from inside the app

roadmap.title: Frames and trusses solved
items: 2D beam and truss elements, sparse solver
Deflected shape, axial, shear and moment diagrams
Reactions and the equilibrium check
Member stresses and utilisation against yield
Verified: cantilever, simply supported beam and a truss against hand calculations

roadmap.title: Parts meshed and solved
items: Automatic triangle meshing with quality refinement and local sizes
6-node triangles (3-node as an option), plane stress and plane strain
Stress and displacement contours, deformed shape, probe, min and max
Verified: plate with a hole, thick cylinder, NAFEMS LE1, patch tests

Materials library from Datum Atlas, with sources
